correctness.rationale: Two-sided stationary Poisson/Markov/Brownian construction gives the marginal resolvent and uniqueness. Conditioning on zero vs positive resets gives exactly the covariance via an exponential integral. Nonzero complex environment eigenvalue produces oscillatory slow tail when r>3nu/2; direct algebra proves positive slow coefficient for r<3nu/2; at equality a sinusoid of exact amplitude 3a²/sqrt13 around offset 10a²/13+4D/r gives the sharp D threshold. Independent RK4 generator equations and direct quadrature agree with closed form within 2.3e-10 over 540 tests; 61 additional boundary checks pass. Numerical samples do not replace analytic universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The proposed contribution is the explicit two-time dot-product covariance and the sharp iff late-negative-lag phase boundary for an autonomous directed three-site environmental target not reset with the particle. The stationary marginal itself follows established random reset-position renewal formulas and is not counted as original. Evans–Majumdar 2011 random-position resets sample independent locations; Rose et al. 2018 reset the entire process to one prescribed state; Julián-Salgado et al. 2023 optimize first-passage statistics for two independent reset locations. Relevant sources and mathematical-record searches did not exhibit the same Markov-correlated triangular reset protocol with exact temporal sign criterion. Residual priority uncertainty remains, especially in specialist hybrid-process literature.

value.rationale: The position-only stationary law exactly hides the environment rotation rate, while a natural measurable two-time position correlation reveals it by infinitely recurring sign reversals. The exact sharp boundary at r=3nu/2 and the strictly positive critical diffusivity are nontrivial structural consequences of competition between reset relaxation and directed Markov cycling. This resolves a motivated finite-state-environment transport question rather than a numerical table or minor coefficient improvement.
